 Oral Judgment
In this appeal, the petitioner is seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Undisputedly, there was an accident on 23.12.2015 at about 7.45 a.m. involving the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-HP-1893 at Basavapattana Village, Kasaba Hobli, Magadi Taluk, in which the petitioner was the NC: 2024:KHC:37705 pillion rider rided by one Ramanna.
Due to capsize of the motorcycle, the petitioner fell down from the motorcycle and sustained head injury.

After taking treatment at Government Hospital, Magadi, Lakshmi Multi Speciality Hospital, Bengaluru under hospitalization, the petitioner through his father approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation of Rs.25,00,000/-.
The claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.

The Tribunal after considering the evidence and on hearing both the parties, by the impugned judgment and award,
awarded the compensation of Rs.13,88,358/- with interest at 8% per annum.
4. The award of the Tribunal is satisfied by the Insurance Company.
Pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement of compensation, the petitioner is before this Court.

sentences.text:
Heard the arguments of Sri Shripad V. Shastri, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri B.
Pradeep, learned counsel for respondent No.2 Insurance Company.
NC: 2024:KHC:37705 6.

It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner has sustained multiple head injuries which affected his future career being a minor boy of 12 years, he has been taken to Chennai for higher treatment, he is having breathlessness, difficulty in opening the mouth to consume the food.
The parents have spent more than two years for taking care of the child leaving behind their earnings.
The compensation assessed by the Tribunal is on the lower side as the medical bills itself is more than Rs.10,50,000/- and sought for enhancement of compensation.

7. Per contra, the learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that the petitioner was 12 years old boy, the accident is of the year 2015, he was under hospitalization for 40 days and compensation awarded by the Tribunal is proportionate to the nature of injuries and money spent towards treatment.
It is further contended that the rate of interest awarded at 8% per annum is on the higher side and no Bank will offer such rate of interest and sought for reduction of interest to 6% per annum.
I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed by learned counsel for both the parties and perused the material on record.
9. The accident is not in dispute.
The Insurance Company admitting its liability has satisfied the award of the Tribunal.
The only point is quantum of compensation.

The medical records show that the petitioner has suffered the following injuries:
1) Comminuted fracture involving antero- lateral posterior and medial walls of both maxilla,
2) Fracture of pterygoid plates of both sides,
3) Fracture of both nasal bones and septum,
4) Fracture alvcolar process of maxilla,
5) Fracture of interior and lateral wall of right orbit,
6) Fracture of mandibular condyles on both sides, and Sri. Dharshan B K vs Palaksha P on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3009146/

sentences.text:
The petitioner was under hospitalization at Lakshmi Multi Speciality Hospital, Bengaluru,
Apollo Hospital, Bengaluru, Panacea Hospital, Bengaluru and NC: 2024:KHC:37705 Santosham Chest hospital, Chennai for more than 40 days.
The medical bills produced to an extent of Rs.12,29,926/-, out of which the Tribunal approved Rs.10,58,358/- with reference to the cross-examination of the father of the petitioner.
Hence, the medical bills has to be kept intact.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.1,00,000/- towards pain and suffering and the same is proper.

The petitioner being a 12 years old boy having sustained severe head injuries with multiple fractures and suffering from breathlessness and noisy breathing problem and he has underwent high risk emergent rigid bronchoscopy and treated at a higher hospital at Chennai for a period from 19.06.2016 to 29.06.2016.

Hence, the petitioner has to be compensated with Rs.2,00,000/- towards loss of amenities and discomfort; incidental expenses such as attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance at Rs.50,000/-; future medical expenses as assessed by P.W.2 doctor Sri C.V.Kumar, Surgeon from Panacea Hospital at Rs.1,00,000/-.
The parents will be laid up for minimum of six months and loss of income at Rs.8,500/- per month for NC: 2024:KHC:37705 six months comes to Rs.51,000/- (Rs.8,500 x 6).
Total compensation comes to Rs.15,59,358/- as against Rs.13,88,358/-, thereby enhancement of Rs.1,71,000/-.
It is the just compensation the petitioner is entitled to in the facts and circumstances of the case.
11. As regarding rate of interest is concerned, as rightly contended by the learned counsel for the Insurance Company, no Bank will offer interest at 8% per annum at relevant point of time.
Since the enhancement is only meager sum of Rs.1,71,000/-, it is not proper to interfere with the discretion of the Tribunal.
Having regard to the nature of injuries and seriousness of the treatment, it is proper to retain the interest at 8% per annum.
12. Hence, appeal merits consideration, in the result, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The impugned judgment and award dated 21.08.2017 passed in M.V.C.No.1274/2016, is modified.
NC: 2024:KHC:37705 (iii) The petitioner is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,71,000/- with interest as awarded by the Tribunal, excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.1,00,000/-.
(iv) The Insurance Company shall deposit the compensation with interest within eight weeks from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this judgment.

SD/-
